title: Teldrassil
body: Teldrassil, whose name means crown of the earth, is the second World Tree of the night elves, rising from the Veiled Sea northwest of Darkshore. After the Battle of Mount Hyjal left Nordrassil scarred and the kaldorei mortal, Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm won the approval of the Circle of Ancients and, with the most powerful druids, grew this new tree in the hope of winning their immortality back. Its upper boughs hold a whole forested land of hills, lakes and streams. Darnassus stands in the west, the village of Dolanaar sits beside the road, the young begin their training in the twilit glade of Shadowglen, and Rut'theran Village at the roots links the island to the mainland. Yet all is not well with the tree, and its growth has proved flawed and unpredictable. Corrupted fel cones drop from its branches, the gentle Gnarlpine furbolgs have turned savage, sick and angry timberlings rise from the soil, and satyrs lurk in its hollows.

parts.body: The root of the trouble, Corithras Moonrage tells, lies with the dragons. Once the tree was grown, Staghelm sought their blessing, as they had blessed Nordrassil in ancient times. Nozdormu, Lord of Time, refused him and chided him for his arrogance, and Alexstrasza agreed and refused as well. Without the blessings of the Life-Binder and the Timeless One, Teldrassil has grown flawed ever since.

title: Shadowglen
body: Ringed by mountains in the northeast of Teldrassil, Shadowglen is a small twilit glade open only to the south, where the road runs down toward Dolanaar. Here young night elves first take up blade, bow and staff under mentors who wait inside the great tree Aldrassil. Even this sheltered place feels the tree's troubles. Conservator Ilthalaine reports that heavy spring rains let the nightsabers and thistle boars multiply beyond what the glade can feed, and grells and grellkin tainted by fel moss creep through the woods. North of Aldrassil lies a moonwell, and a phial of its water is the first step of the long lesson Tenaron Stormgrip sets for every pupil.

title: Aldrassil
body: At the heart of Shadowglen rises Aldrassil, a great tree within the World Tree, its hollow levels home to the trainers who teach each new generation of night elf warriors, hunters, rogues, priests and druids. Sigils sent from inside its walls call the young to their first lessons, reminding them that their people have rejoined the other races of Azeroth and now need protectors of every kind. Mardant Strongoak guides young druids near the top of the tree, and the highest room belongs to Tenaron Stormgrip, who leads Shadowglen. A visiting scholar, Gilshalan Windwalker, works here too, studying the webwood spiders to learn how the new tree has changed them.

title: Shadowthread Cave
body: On the northern edge of Shadowglen opens the Shadowthread Cave, a lair of webwood spiders. They are cousins of a far smaller breed, and the scholar Gilshalan Windwalker believes the growth of the new World Tree has swollen them to their present size; he seeks their venom and an egg from the nest deep inside to prove it. The cave is a real danger to the careless. The young elf Iverron spends much of his time near its mouth, and today his friend Dirania Silvershine, who sees him at the same hour every day, waits for him in the glade and wonders why he is several hours late.

It reached Iverron in time. He is always getting into trouble, he admits, and Dirania always gets him out of it. He feels much better, though he means to sit a while longer, and hopes someone will clear him a path through the spiders first.

title: Starbreeze Village
body: Starbreeze is a quiet hamlet of a few small night elf houses near a moonwell in eastern Teldrassil, southeast of Shadowglen and east of Dolanaar. Its peace is gone. The Gnarlpine furbolgs, once gentle, have overrun it, and Gnarlpine warriors, gardeners and ursas now roam among the homes, among them a dangerous brute called Uruson. Gaerolas Talvethren, Great Warden of the sleeping Druids of the Talon, keeps to the village, and in Dolanaar the druid Athridas Bearmantle waits uneasily for word from him. When the furbolgs took the village, Tallonkai Swiftroot had to leave a treasured emerald dreamcatcher behind in his dresser here.

parts.body: Gaerolas has been badly hurt. Too wounded to carry the news to Athridas himself, the warden can only hope the furbolgs have not yet reached the barrow.

title: Dolanaar
body: Dolanaar is the first true town on the road south from Shadowglen, a night elf village in central Teldrassil gathered about a moonwell. Its inn offers rest under Elune's watch, and its trainers carry on the lessons begun at Aldrassil. It is also where the troubles of the forest are weighed. Corithras Moonrage tends the moonwell and tells the story of the tree's making, the druid Athridas Bearmantle watches over the slumbering Druids of the Talon, and Tallonkai Swiftroot quietly wants a satyr lord hiding just to the north put down. Sentinels keep watch over the village, and Moon Priestess Amara watches the road west to Darnassus.

title: Fel Rock
body: Just north of Dolanaar lies Fel Rock, a cave whose old beauty has given way to corruption. The satyr Lord Melenas has made it his lair and gathered a large band of grell warriors about him, joined by shadow, rascal and dark sprites, and a rare, brutish grell called Threggil prowls among them. In Dolanaar, Tallonkai Swiftroot treats Melenas as a shameful secret, a satyr far too close to home, and asks those he sends into the cave to settle the matter quickly and quietly.

title: Lake Al'Ameth
body: South of Dolanaar spreads Lake Al'Ameth, one of the largest lakes on Teldrassil. Its shores have grown unsafe, for the timberlings, elementals of nature that mirror the health of the tree's plants and animals, have turned angry, and diseased sprouts keep springing up along the water faster than they can be cleared. The herbalist Denalan keeps a small camp on the eastern shore with a planter of specially prepared soil, testing seeds, fronds and fruit in search of a cure, and hoping to solve the riddle of what taints the timberlings. A cave opens on the lake's southern bank.

title: Ban'ethil Hollow
body: West of Dolanaar, below the road to Darnassus, lies Ban'ethil Hollow. It now belongs to the Gnarlpine, whose shamans, augurs and defenders crowd its slopes, while ambushers creep up from their den to fall on travelers bound for the capital. News and trade pass along that road every day, and the Sentinels of Teldrassil reward anyone who thins the ambushers' ranks. Somewhere within the hollow lies the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, a sacred resting place of the Druids of the Talon that the furbolgs have overrun.

title: Ban'ethil Barrow Den
body: The Ban'ethil Barrow Den is one of the sacred places the night elves built to shelter the Druids of the Talon while they sleep, their spirits walking the Emerald Dream in keeping with a pact with Ysera. Its keepers stored the Relics of Wakening, a talisman, a quill, a sapphire and a rune, in chests within, for the hibernation cannot be broken safely without them. Gnarlpine invaders have since ransacked the den. Their shamans have even learned to part a sleeping druid's spirit from his body: the spirit of Oben Rageclaw wanders the barrow, powerless, while his own animated form guards its deepest chambers against intruders.

title: Gnarlpine Hold
body: In the far southwest of Teldrassil lies Gnarlpine Hold, home of the Gnarlpine furbolgs. They were once a peaceful people and friends of the night elves, but fel moss has driven them mad, and here their chieftain, Ursal the Mauler, holds sway over a tribe in frenzy. Pathfinders, avengers and totemics guard the hold, along with a hulking brute named Grimmaw. Among them lie enslaved Druids of the Talon, sunk in sleep and held captive by the furbolgs.

title: Pools of Arlithrien
body: The Pools of Arlithrien are a scatter of small pools in western Teldrassil, just southeast of the entrance to Darnassus. Once a peaceful spot, they are now prowled by nightsaber stalkers and webwood spiders, and the Gnarlpine have pressed so close that the Sentinels struggle to patrol the area. A lone moonwell still stands on the shore. Its water is still needed by the druids of Darnassus, but those who come to fill a phial are warned to keep their weapons close at hand.

title: Wellspring Lake
body: Southeast of the Oracle Glade and northeast of Darnassus, Wellspring Lake is fed by a spring deep within the World Tree and drains away along the Wellspring River. The night elves once came here to fish, but the timberlings that wander its waters are the most tainted on the island, studded with mossy tumors, and the druids have ordered them cut down so the tumors can be burned. Along the river gather elder timberlings and mire beasts, and among them moves a foul timberling called Blackmoss the Fetid.

title: The Oracle Glade
body: In the northwest of Teldrassil stands the Oracle Tree, an ancient and wise presence that watches over the growth of Teldrassil alongside the druids and sends its reports to the Arch Druid on shed pieces of inscribed bark. Beneath its boughs lies the first and most powerful moonwell on the island. Bloodfeather harpies have built their nests all around the glade, and when the tree sent a runner to Darnassus, the harpies killed the messenger. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak and a small band of Sentinels hold the moonwell and push the harpies back little by little. On a branch at the glade's edge dwells the reclusive satyr Sethir the Ancient.

title: Rut'theran Village
body: Rut'theran Village sits among the roots of Teldrassil on the shore of the Veiled Sea, the island's link to the mainland. A portal carries travelers up to Darnassus, a ferry sails to Auberdine in Darkshore, and hippogryphs fly constantly between the village and the far shore, while Erelas Ambersky trains and cares for the young birds. The waters here are astonishingly rich. Fish caught off Teldrassil grow to nearly twice the size of their mainland kin, and Nessa Shadowsong and the other villagers suspect the swift growth of the World Tree itself. Daryn Lightwind, a lore keeper of the Cenarion Circle, keeps her piles of books here, among them a history of Feralas.

title: Tenaron Stormgrip
body: Tenaron Stormgrip leads Shadowglen from the highest room atop Aldrassil, and he summons each promising young night elf before they set out into the wider world. He holds that none should leave the enchanted forests without first understanding their people's recent history: the Battle of Mount Hyjal, Nordrassil left a pale shadow after its power was spent against Archimonde, and the moonwells that hold the waters of the ancient Well of Eternity, which the druids use and the Sentinels revere, though sorcery stays forbidden to all. He begins that lesson with a single phial from the moonwell north of Aldrassil, then sends his pupils south to Corithras Moonrage.

title: Corithras Moonrage
body: Corithras Moonrage tends the moonwell of Dolanaar and carries on the telling that Tenaron Stormgrip begins in Shadowglen. The druids of Darnassus use the waters of Teldrassil's moonwells, and their own well must be replenished from time to time, so Corithras gives young messengers specially crafted phials and sends them out to the moonwells of Starbreeze Village, the Pools of Arlithrien and the Oracle Glade. Each time one returns, he takes up the story of how the night elves came to their new home where he last left off, one chapter for every phial.
sources: quest 928 (Corithras at the moonwell in Dolanaar)
quests 929, 933, 7383 (descriptions and reward texts: the telling, Betrayer freed, Shan'do Stormrage disappeared, Staghelm and the Circle, Nozdormu and Alexstrasza refuse)
quest 935 description (flawed growth, strange beasts, crazed furbolgs, filled vessel for Fandral)
quest 929 description (druids in Darnassus use the water)
quest 933 completion text (furbolg reports at first dismissed)
quest 7383 description (a problem he will not get into yet)
notes: Checked: The chapters (929 and 933 reward texts) moved from the opening to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 933 (933 follows 929), with the dismissed furbolg reports (933 completion text) and the problem held back (7383 description, offered on the 933 turn-in); a newcomer hears none of them before those turn-ins. The opening is the errand (929 description). Converted: the dragons' refusal (withheld by Corithras until the last phial, 7383 description) and the filled vessel for Fandral moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 7383, after which he offers 935. The earlier chapters stay in the opening as the shared history the zone entry also tells. 935 itself is left to Darnassus. Earlier: Faction 1: Darnassus faction template 80. Verified.

parts.body: His chapters tell of a people adrift. After Hyjal the night elves lost their immortality, the Betrayer was freed from his prison, and Malfurion Stormrage vanished, never to return. Fandral Staghelm took up the leadership of the druids, persuaded the Circle of Ancients that it was time to rebuild, and grew Teldrassil. Corithras does not hide that the new home is troubled, and admits that the first reports of crazed furbolgs were dismissed. One problem he holds back for the last phial.
sources: quest 929 reward text
quest 933 reward and completion texts
quest 7383 description (offered on the 933 turn-in)

parts.body: With the water of the Oracle Glade before him, Corithras finishes the tale. Staghelm sought the dragons' blessing for the tree, but Nozdormu refused and chided him for his arrogance, and Alexstrasza refused as well. Without them Teldrassil's growth has been flawed, breeding strange beasts and crazed furbolgs, and Corithras pours all the phials together into one vessel for the Arch Druid in Darnassus.
sources: quest 7383 reward text
quest 935 description (offered on the 7383 turn-in: flawed growth, strange beasts, crazed furbolgs, filled vessel for Fandral)

title: Athridas Bearmantle
body: The druid Athridas Bearmantle of Dolanaar shares the dryad Tarindrella's concern for the well being of the forest, and he keeps watch over his brethren the Druids of the Talon, who slumber in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den with their spirits in the Emerald Dream, keeping a pact with Ysera. Their safety rests with the Great Warden, Gaerolas Talvethren of Starbreeze Village, but word from Gaerolas is late in coming, and Athridas has grown uneasy. He seeks someone to travel east and bring back the warden's report, so that he may know his dreaming brethren slumber safely.
sources: quest 459 reward text (Athridas shares our concern for the well being of the forest)
quest 475 description (word from Gaerolas delayed, dreaming brethren)
quest 475 reward text (I knew Athridas would sense trouble and send help)
quests 476, 483, 486 (grave news, Relics of Wakening, ritual needs Ursal slain)
notes: Checked: The kidnapped druids (483 completion text, seen on returning to turn 483 in) moved from part 1 (DONE 476, ACCEPT 483) to part 2 (DONE 483, ACCEPT 486). Converted: the grave news and the relics moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 476, QUEST_ACCEPT 483), the recovered relics and Ursal's part to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 483, QUEST_ACCEPT 486), the ritual completed to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 486). The opening is the premise of 475. Earlier: Faction 1: Darnassus faction template 80. The wiki's guess that he is related to Broll Bearmantle is not used. Verified.

parts.body: Athridas sensed rightly that something was wrong, and the news that comes back is grave. The Gnarlpine have been corrupted, Gaerolas lies wounded, and furbolg invaders have been seen ravaging the barrow. Unless they are woken, the sleepers will stay trapped in the Dream forever, and their hibernation cannot be broken without the Relics of Wakening, kept in the den's sacred chests, so Athridas sends for the relics.
sources: quest 475 reward text (I knew Athridas would sense trouble)
quest 476 description and reward text
quest 483 description

parts.body: The relics come back to him just in time, for the furbolgs have kidnapped some of the sleeping druids, and Athridas prepares the ritual of awakening. Yet it can take effect only once the cursed beast responsible is slain: Ursal the Mauler, the Gnarlpine chieftain who meddled with the sleepers' calling, must die at Gnarlpine Hold before his brethren can be freed.
sources: quest 483 completion text (kidnapped Druids of the Talon) and reward text
quest 486 description

parts.body: With Ursal slain, the ritual is complete. Athridas hails the one who did it as a most worthy night elf, sure to find great glory by following the path of honor, and asks the forest spirits to guard them wherever they go.
sources: quest 486 reward text

title: Tarindrella
body: Tarindrella is a dryad, a mysterious woodland protector whose presence had not been felt in the forests of Kalimdor for years. Her sudden return to Shadowglen, southwest of Aldrassil, reached the druid Melithar Staghelm through the whisperings of the forest spirits, and he took it as a sure sign that something was amiss. She has come because of a gathering evil. The peaceful furbolgs of the hills are deserting their homes and massing as the Gnarlpine tribe, and she believes only the wicked fel moss could cause such a change. The grells and grellkin now threatening Shadowglen may show whether she is right.
sources: quest 458 description (Melithar: dryad Tarindrella returned, not felt in Kalimdor in years, southwest of Aldrassil)
quest 459 description and reward text (Gnarlpine amassing, Fel Moss, grells tainted, seek out Athridas)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Tarindrella (dryad, returned to investigate corruption)
notes: Converted: the confirmation (grells tainted) and the referral to Athridas moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 459; the opening keeps her suspicion (459 description). Earlier: Faction 1: Darnassus faction template 80. She directs the messenger to Athridas rather than sending word herself; reworded.

parts.body: The grells prove to be tainted by the fel moss, and her fears are confirmed. If even the grells have fallen to it, she says, one can only imagine what has become of the Gnarlpine, and she points the way to Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar, who shares her concern for the well being of the forest.
sources: quest 459 reward text

title: Denalan
body: Denalan is a night elf herbalist who has pitched his camp on the eastern shore of Lake Al'Ameth to study the plant life of Teldrassil. The tree's creation was a grand achievement, he says, but now the world must shift to regain its balance. Believing the soil itself is what angers the timberlings, he works with rare earths sent from Darnassus and a planter of specially prepared soil, and he tests strange plants, one like nothing he has seen since a journey to the Swamp of Sorrows decades ago. He shares his work with his friend Rellian Greenspyre, a druid of Darnassus with ideas of his own about the timberlings.
sources: quest_greeting 2080 (creation of Teldrassil a grand achievement, world must shift to regain balance)
quests 918, 997 (soil theory, rare earths, camp on the eastern end of the lake)
quests 930, 931 reward texts (exotic fruit, frond from the Swamp of Sorrows)
quest 941, gameobject 7923 Denalan's Planter
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Denalan (herbalist, eastern edge of Lake Al'Ameth)
quest 922 description (Rellian's interest, ideas of his own)
notes: Converted: Rellian's 'only hope' line (922 reward text, a Darnassus turn-in) left the opening; it is told in part 1 on QUEST_ACCEPT 2499, which can only be reached after 922, 923 and 2498, together with Oakenscowl as the source. Oakenscowl's end and Denalan's verdict moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 2499). quest_greeting 2080 reread: classic. Earlier: Faction 1: Darnassus faction template 80; 2499 is offered by him. Swamp of Sorrows line narrowed to what quest 931 says.

parts.body: Rellian's verdict on the seeds was bleak: the taint of the corrupted timberlings passes into their seeds, beyond his skill to mend, and Denalan, he said, may be their only hope. Soon after, Denalan found what may be the cause. In a cave on the lake's southern bank, the timberling Oakenscowl, poisoned by a gargantuan tumor, is spreading corruption to every creature of the lake.
sources: quest 922 reward text (reached only through 922, 923, 2498 before 2499)
quest 2498 description
quest 2499 description

parts.body: Oakenscowl falls, and Denalan takes the great tumor to study the disease that upsets the timberlings. It is a distressing thing, he says, for Oakenscowl was once a grand leader among his kind, but corruption does not discriminate between the lowly and the noble.
sources: quest 2499 reward text

title: Zenn Foulhoof
body: Zenn Foulhoof is a satyr who lingers on the outskirts of Dolanaar, all charm and promises of things beyond imagining for any young adventurer willing to run his errands. What he wants are fangs, feathers and silk taken from the creatures of the forest, reagents, he says, for his business in the woods, and he would like it all kept a little secret between friends. Satyrs are an old shame to the night elves, so it is a curious thing to find one waiting so openly beside a night elf village, smiling and making his offers.
sources: quest 488 description and reward text (fangs, feathers, silk, reagents, three cheers for the naive and gullible)
quest 489 description (Council of the Forest, Fel Cones, harmless snack)
creature_text 2150 (Ribbit! ... You have duped me)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Zenn_Foulhoof (satyr east of Dolanaar, turned into a frog)
quest 932 description (the satyr are an embarrassment to the night elves)
notes: Checked: The Council's verdict (satyr an enemy of the forest, killing nature's creatures; 489 description, offered after 488) moved from the opening to part 2 (DONE 489); the opening keeps only the general standing of satyrs (932) and what is seen. Converted: his gloating moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 488); the Council's demand and the frog moved to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 489, which stays an entry trigger too). The opening is the premise of 488 plus the satyr's standing from 489's description. creature_text 2150 reread: classic. Earlier: verified. Faction 1: Zenn uses faction template 80.

parts.body: Once he has his reagents, Zenn crows with delight. Who would have guessed, he laughs, that he would have such a helper to do his bidding? The world is full of surprises, and he raises three cheers for the naive and gullible.
sources: quest 488 reward text

parts.body: The Council of the Forest learns who helped him and demands redemption. The satyr is an enemy of the forest, it declares, and killing nature's creatures for him defiles it. Its price is a lesson for Zenn: a handful of fel cones, the corrupted seeds that fall smoking from the trees, offered as a harmless snack. He takes them gladly. One taste turns him into a croaking frog, wailing between ribbits that he has been duped by foul trickery.
sources: quest 489 description
creature_text 2150 (Ribbit! ... You have duped me), smart_scripts 2150 on 489 finished

title: Ursal the Mauler
body: Ursal the Mauler is the chieftain of the Gnarlpine furbolgs, ruling them from Gnarlpine Hold in the far southwest of Teldrassil. His once peaceful tribe has fallen into madness, and his pathfinders, avengers and totemics guard the hold, beside a hulking brute named Grimmaw. Among them, enslaved and sunk in sleep, lie Druids of the Talon held captive by the furbolgs. Ursal himself is a savage fighter who mauls any who come against him.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Ursal_the_Mauler
zone_areas: Gnarlpine Pathfinder, Avenger, Totemic, Grimmaw 14429, Enslaved Druid of the Talon 2852 in area 261
smart_scripts 2039 (casts Maul)
creature 2852 Enslaved Druid of the Talon: friendly (faction 35), sleeping stand state (creature_template_addon bytes1 3)
Ursal 2039 spawns in area 261, so a bystander at the kill has the Gnarlpine Hold opening (14110) too
notes: Checked: creature_text 2852 is never said (no smart_scripts or core script for 2852, nothing on Ursal's death), so the captives' cry was removed; part 3 (KILL 2039, DONE 486) now tells only the fall a bystander sees. The opening no longer says where the captives came from (483 completion text). Converted for group kill credit: the opening (KILL 2039 or ACCEPT 486) now tells only what is seen at the hold. Ursal as master of the fel moss, the ambush and the pillage moved to part 1 (QUEST_ACCEPT 476); his meddling with the sleepers and the ritual to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 486); the captives' cry to part 3 (KILL 2039, QUEST_DONE 486). Unsure: creature_text 2852 has no script in this DB that makes the druids say it on his death. Faction 0: Ursal uses faction template 82, hostile to all; parts 1 and 2 are Alliance-only routes. Earlier: Faction 0: Ursal uses faction template 82, hostile to all players; Horde reach Teldrassil by the Auberdine boat and the Rut'theran portal (areatrigger 542 has no faction limit). Verified.

parts.body: It is Ursal who wields the evil power of the fel moss to drive his tribe mad, so the wounded warden Gaerolas Talvethren reports, and under him the furbolgs ambushed Gaerolas on his way to the Barrow Den and pillaged Starbreeze Village.
sources: quest 476 description

parts.body: The druids of Dolanaar lay a heavier charge on him. It was Ursal who meddled with the calling of the sleeping Druids of the Talon, and Athridas Bearmantle holds that the ritual to wake them cannot succeed while he lives.
sources: quest 486 description

parts.body: In the end Ursal the Mauler is brought down in the heart of Gnarlpine Hold, fighting savagely to the last, and the frenzied furbolgs who guard it are left without the chieftain who ruled them.
sources: smart_scripts 2039 (casts Maul in combat)
DB spawns: Ursal 2039 and his guards in area 261

title: Lord Melenas
body: Satyrs are an old shame to the night elves, and Lord Melenas is a shame far too close to home. From the cave of Fel Rock, just north of Dolanaar, this vicious satyr has gathered a large band of grell warriors, and his heart is said to be black as night as he plots something foul. Tallonkai Swiftroot of Dolanaar would rather the matter stayed between trusted friends. He asks that Melenas be dealt with quickly and quietly, before more is made of it, and wants only the satyr's head as proof that the embarrassment is ended.
sources: quest 932 description, request text and reward text
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Lord_Melenas (vicious satyr, small army of grells, deep in Fel Rock)
DB: Lord Melenas 2038 has three possible spawn points inside Fel Rock
notes: Unchanged in the parts conversion: nothing to hide. No outcome told: the opening (KILL 2038, ACCEPT 932) is Tallonkai's premise for 932 and what is seen at Fel Rock. Earlier: Faction 0: Melenas uses faction template 90, hostile to all players, and Horde could reach Teldrassil in 3.3.5 by the Auberdine boat and the Rut'theran portal. Tallonkai's class is not stated in game data, so 'a druid' was dropped.

title: Oben Rageclaw
body: Oben Rageclaw was a druid of the Claw who slept in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den when the Gnarlpine came. Their shamans have discovered how to separate a sleeping druid's spirit from his body, and they did so to Oben, animating his empty form and turning it against anyone who explores the den. His spirit lingers in the barrow, trapped in the Emerald Dream and powerless to stop it. The shamans carry a strange charm for the ritual, and Oben hopes that by examining one he may learn how to break the enchantment.
sources: quest 2541 description (shamans separate spirit from body, animated form attacks explorers, trapped in the Emerald Dream)
quest 2561 description and reward (kill my physical form, use the charm, rest peacefully in the Emerald Dream)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Oben_Rageclaw (night elf ghost, druid of the claw, body Rageclaw 7318)
notes: Converted: his only way out (kill his own body, use the charm) moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 2541, QUEST_ACCEPT 2561); his release added as part 2 (QUEST_DONE 2561, from the reward text already cited). The opening is 2541's premise. Earlier: Faction 1: creature 7317 uses faction template 80. Verified.

parts.body: The charm gives off a vile aura, a very powerful enchantment, and having studied it, Oben sees only one way out. His soulless body, in the deepest part of the den, must be slain and the charm used on its fallen form. He regrets asking it, but there is no other way to escape the Gnarlpine's control.
sources: quest 2541 reward text
quest 2561 description

parts.body: It is done. Free at last of the Gnarlpine, Oben's spirit may rest peacefully forever in the Emerald Dream, and he parts from his helper with thanks and the hope that they may one day meet again.
sources: quest 2561 reward text

title: Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak
body: Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak was sent with a small group of Sentinels to protect the sanctity of the Oracle Glade from the Bloodfeather harpies nesting all around it. She holds her post at the moonwell beneath the Oracle Tree and drives the harpies back a little at a time. The task is a grim one: when the Oracle Tree tried to send a runner to Darnassus with a report, the harpies attacked and killed the messenger. Arynia has faith in those who take up the fight beside her, though the harpies' slashing talons and piercing beaks are no easy match.
sources: quest_greeting 3519 (tasked with protecting the sanctity of the Oracle Grove)
quest 937 description and completion text (small group of Sentinels, push the harpies back, runner killed, talons and beaks)
notes: Converted: Mist's capture and return moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 938 (turned in to Arynia; her words on the capture are its completion text); the opening keeps her post and the harpies (937). ACCEPT 938 stays an entry trigger. quest_greeting and creature_text 3519, 3568 reread: classic. Earlier: Faction 1: Arynia and Mist (quest 938 starter) use faction template 80. Verified.

parts.body: Her loss was a personal one as well. Her gray sabercat companion, Mist, was taken when the harpy witches caught Arynia off guard, and she blamed herself, believing Mist dead. The cat lived, though cruelly wounded, and found her way back with a stranger's help. Arynia's joy at the reunion is matched only by her gratitude.
sources: quest 938 description, completion and reward texts
creature_text 3519, 3568

title: Sethir the Ancient
body: On a branch at the outskirts of the Oracle Glade, far from any other creature, lives a lone satyr known as Sethir the Ancient. Satyrs are an old shame to the night elves, and to find one dwelling in the boughs of the new World Tree is troubling in itself. Sethir gathers no followers about him, as Lord Melenas does at Fel Rock, and keeps only his solitary perch, meeting any who come near with open hostility. What drew him there he keeps to himself.
sources: quest 2242 description (hides on a branch at the outskirts of the Oracle Glade)
DB spawn: Sethir 6909 alone at 11078, 1902 (area 141), no other creature within 80 yards; creature_template faction 14, hostile to all
quest 932 description (the satyr are an embarrassment; Melenas has gathered grell warriors)
notes: Checked: For the KILL-only trigger: the rogues' belief and that all who approached him died (2242 description, a Darnassus quest) removed; the rants removed because creature_text 6909 is never said (no smart_scripts or core script, no AIName). The journal is pickpocket loot for 2242, so Darnassus keeps it. Converted for group kill credit and ownership: the journal and its link to the sickness of Darkshore (the 2242 reward text, Syurna's verdict, which Darnassus owns) dropped, since no Teldrassil trigger reaches it and a bystander at the KILL never sees the journal. Unsure: creature_text 6909 has no script in this DB, so the rants may never be heard in game. Earlier: Faction 0: Sethir uses faction template 14, hostile to all players, reachable by Horde as for Ursal. Quests 2241 and 2242 are left free for Darnassus. Verified.

title: Crown of the Earth
body: Before the young of Shadowglen go out into the world, they are sent to learn their people's recent history and how their new home came to be. Tenaron Stormgrip begins with the Battle of Mount Hyjal, after which Nordrassil was left a pale shadow of itself, and with the moonwells, which hold the waters of the ancient Well of Eternity. He asks for a phial from the moonwell north of Aldrassil and sends it on to Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. Corithras sends the messenger in turn to the moonwells of Starbreeze Village, the Pools of Arlithrien and finally the Oracle Glade, for the druids of Darnassus need the waters for their own well. With each phial he carries the story on where Tenaron left off.
sources: quests 920, 921, 928, 929, 933, 7383, 935 (descriptions, request and reward texts)
quest 929 description (the druids in Darnassus use moonwell water, their moonwell must be replenished)
notes: Checked: Corithras's chapters are told only at the turn-ins (929 reward: immortality lost, the Betrayer freed, Malfurion gone; 933 reward: Fandral and the Circle grow the tree), so they moved from the opening to parts 1 (DONE 929) and 2 (DONE 933); the problem held back (7383 description) moved to part 2; the dragons are now part 3 (DONE 7383). The opening keeps Tenaron's lesson (921 description and completion text) and the errand (929 description). Converted: the dragons' refusal (the problem withheld in 7383's description) and the filled vessel moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 7383. The delivery to Fandral and his reply (935 turn-in) stay with Darnassus, so the chain's ending is no longer told here. Earlier: Chain 920 > 921 > 928 > 929 > 933 > 7383 > 935. Quest 934 is an unused duplicate of 7383 with no giver. The final quest 935 is turned in to Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus and is left free as a trigger for the Darnassus writer. Verified.

parts.body: With the water of Starbreeze, the telling begins in earnest. After Hyjal, Corithras says, the night elves were left without direction. Nordrassil smoked from the fire it had unleashed, and their immortality, the very essence of their being, was lost. In that dark time the Betrayer was freed from his prison, and Shan'do Stormrage disappeared.
sources: quest 929 reward text

parts.body: The second phial brings the next chapter. Malfurion never returned, and to this day no one knows what became of him. With the druids in disarray, Fandral Staghelm took up their leadership and convinced the Circle of Ancients that the time had come to rebuild and regain their immortality, and with the Circle's approval he and the most powerful druids grew Teldrassil. Yet all was not well, Corithras admits: one small problem lies behind many of the tree's troubles, and that he saves for the last well.
sources: quest 933 reward text
quest 7383 description (offered on the 933 turn-in)

parts.body: With the water of the Oracle Glade, the first and most powerful well, Corithras reaches the heart of the tale. Once the tree was grown, Staghelm sought the dragons' blessing, as they had blessed Nordrassil of old, but Nozdormu refused, chiding him for his arrogance, and Alexstrasza agreed and refused as well. Teldrassil has grown flawed and unpredictable ever since. Corithras pours all the phials together into one vessel, to be carried to the Arch Druid in Darnassus.
sources: quest 7383 reward text
quest 935 description (offered on the 7383 turn-in)

title: The Sleepers of Ban'ethil
body: The first sign comes to Shadowglen, where the dryad Tarindrella returns after years away and fears that fel moss has corrupted the peaceful furbolgs, who are massing as the Gnarlpine tribe. In Dolanaar, Athridas Bearmantle has his own worry. The Druids of the Talon sleep in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, their spirits walking the Emerald Dream under a pact with Ysera, and their Great Warden, Gaerolas Talvethren of Starbreeze Village, keeps them safe. But word from Gaerolas is late, and Athridas sends for news.
sources: quests 458, 459 (Tarindrella, Fel Moss, grells, Athridas)
quests 475, 476, 483, 486 (descriptions, request and reward texts)
notes: Checked: Part 4 no longer rests on creature_text 2852 (never said: no script); it ends on what 486 promises. The kidnapping (483 completion text) moved from part 3 (DONE 476, ACCEPT 483) to part 4. Converted: Tarindrella's confirmation to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 459), Gaerolas's report to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 476), the ravaged barrow and the relics to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 476, QUEST_ACCEPT 483), the ritual and Ursal's death to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 486). Entry points unchanged (ACCEPT 458, 475); a character who starts at 475 skips part 1, and part 2 still reads on from the opening. Earlier: Two entry points: 458 in Shadowglen (Melithar Staghelm, leading through 459 to Athridas) and 475 in Dolanaar. Verified.

parts.body: Tarindrella's fears prove true: the grells of Shadowglen are tainted by the fel moss, and if even they have fallen to it, the Gnarlpine can only be worse. She sends her helper on to Athridas, who shares her concern.
sources: quest 459 reward text

parts.body: Gaerolas is found at Starbreeze, badly wounded. The Gnarlpine ambushed him as he left for the barrow and then sacked the village, maddened by their chieftain, Ursal the Mauler, and his fel moss. Too hurt to travel, the warden can only hope the furbolgs have not yet reached the den.
sources: quest 476 description

parts.body: They have. Gnarlpine invaders have been seen ravaging the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, and unless its sleepers are woken they will stay lost in the Dream forever, unaware of their fate. The delicate hibernation cannot be broken without the four Relics of Wakening, a talisman, a quill, a sapphire and a rune, which the druids keep in the den's sacred chests.
sources: quest 483 description

parts.body: The relics are recovered just in time, though the furbolgs have carried off some of the sleepers, and Athridas prepares the ritual of awakening. It can take hold only once the one who meddled with the sleepers' calling is slain. Ursal the Mauler falls at Gnarlpine Hold, and with his death nothing more stands between the ritual and the freeing of the captive druids.
sources: quest 483 completion text (kidnapped Druids of the Talon) and reward text
quest 486 description (only then will the ritual be complete, so they can be freed)

title: The Tainted Timberlings
body: The timberlings of Teldrassil mirror the health of its plants and beasts, and they have grown angry. Denalan, camped on Lake Al'Ameth, suspects the soil. With rare earths from Darnassus and a planter of specially prepared soil, he plants seeds gathered from the lake's timberlings in hope of growing a gentler generation, while the sickly sprouts along the shore must be pulled up before they grow large enough to cause trouble. They are spreading at a dangerous rate, and Denalan longs to solve the riddle of what taints them. One of the seeds goes to his friend Rellian Greenspyre, a druid of Darnassus who has ideas of his own.
sources: quests 997, 918, 919, 922, 923, 2498, 2499 (descriptions, request and reward texts)
quests 927, 941 (heart, moss removed, planted, emerges cleansed)
notes: Checked: 'Looks much like a seed' removed: creature_text 2080 line 8 is not said by any script (Denalan's smart_scripts cover 997, 930, 931 only); part 3 now follows the 941 description and reward text. Converted: Rellian's findings and Oakenscowl as the source moved to part 1 on QUEST_ACCEPT 2499 (the Darnassus steps 922, 923, 2498 cannot carry triggers here, and 2499 can only be taken after them); Oakenscowl's end to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 2499); the heart of Blackmoss to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 941, at the planter). Unsure: a character who turns in 922 and 923 in Darnassus but never returns to Denalan sees Rellian's findings in no Teldrassil part. Earlier: 'Proves to be a seed' softened to what Denalan says (it looks like a seed). Otherwise verified; 922, 923, 2498 left free for Darnassus.

parts.body: Rellian's answer is bleak. The parents' taint passes into their seeds, beyond his power to mend, and the worst afflicted, the timberlings of Wellspring Lake, must be cut down and their mossy tumors burned. Then word comes that Denalan has found what may be the cause: Oakenscowl, bloated by a gargantuan tumor in a cave on the lake's southern bank, spreading corruption to every creature of the lake.
sources: quests 922, 923 reward texts and 2498 description (all reached before 2499)
quest 2499 description

parts.body: Oakenscowl falls and his tumor is carried to Denalan for study. It is a distressing end, he says, for Oakenscowl was once a grand leader among his kind, but corruption does not discriminate between the lowly and the noble.
sources: quest 2499 reward text

parts.body: Even the heart of Blackmoss the Fetid, sheathed in dark, oily moss and still beating after his death, finds its way to Denalan. He scrapes the foul moss away, but the heart remains tainted. Placed in his planter of prepared soil, it quickly digs itself in, and moments later it wriggles back out, cleansed and faintly pulsing.
sources: quest 927 description and reward text
quest 941 description and reward text (turned in at gameobject 7923 Denalan's Planter)

title: The Emerald Dreamcatcher
body: Tallonkai Swiftroot of Dolanaar was once given an emerald dreamcatcher by Gaerolas Talvethren, warden of the sleeping druids, a gift granted to few: an amulet able to draw energy from the Emerald Dream and bring luck to whoever carries it. When the Gnarlpine overran Starbreeze Village, the dreamcatcher was left behind in Tallonkai's dresser there, and he has not been able to retrieve it. Starbreeze was once a tranquil place, and he can only hope the furbolgs have left his treasure unharmed.
sources: quest 2438 description and reward text (gift from Gaerolas, siphons energy from the Emerald Dream, luck, dresser in Starbreeze, a gift only given to few)
quest 2459 description (emerald missing, Ferocitas north of Starbreeze, necklace glows green, power useless to him, kill mystics)
DB: Ferocitas 7234 and Gnarlpine Mystic 7235 spawns north of Starbreeze
notes: Converted: the damaged dreamcatcher and Ferocitas moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 2438, QUEST_ACCEPT 2459); the emerald recovered to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 2459). Earlier: Chain 2438 > 2459. Verified.

parts.body: The dreamcatcher comes back damaged, its emerald gone. Reports place the stone with Ferocitas the Dream Eater, leader of a band of Gnarlpine mystics north of Starbreeze, who has been seen wearing a necklace that glows green in the night. The jewel's power is useless to the furbolg, but Tallonkai will not rest until his gift is whole.
sources: quest 2459 description

parts.body: The mystics pay for the theft, and the missing emerald is taken back from Ferocitas the Dream Eater, whose wearing of it never gave him any of its power. With the jewel in hand at last, Tallonkai can repair his treasured dreamcatcher, the gift of Gaerolas.
sources: quest 2459 reward text

title: The Oracle's Messenger
body: The Oracle Tree watches over Teldrassil's growth beside the druids, sending its reports to the Arch Druid in Darnassus. But its latest report never arrived. Bloodfeather harpies have nested all around its glade, and when the tree sent a runner to the capital, the harpies cut the messenger down. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak and her small band can only push them back a little at a time, and she asks for help in raiding the nests, with the harpies' belts brought back as proof.
sources: quest 937 description and reward text (harpies, runner killed, the Oracle Tree shed a piece of its bark)
quest 7383 completion text (the Oracle Tree monitors Teldrassil's growth)
notes: Checked: Confirmed the greater calm and the forest's promise are only in the 940 description (Darnassus-owned); 'as the glade grows quiet' in part 1, which echoed it, replaced. Converted: the harpies driven off and the shed bark moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 937. The tree's own message (940 description, offered by Arynia afterwards) and Fandral's reading of the report (940 reward text) are dropped: 940 belongs to Darnassus, so no Teldrassil trigger can carry them. Earlier: Chain 937 > 940 > 952. 940 is turned in to Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus and is left free as a trigger for the Darnassus writer; 952 continues to Onu in Darkshore. Mist (938) is covered under Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak. Verified.

parts.body: The harpies are driven from their nests, and Arynia marvels at how much was done in so short a time, though she knows greater tasks lie ahead for the one who did it. Soon after, the Oracle Tree sheds a piece of its bark. No doubt, Arynia says, the tree has a task it wishes completed.
sources: quest 937 reward text
